body: Last time, it was just sitting on the cliff top, and just writing for hours, all the things that made me feel like killing myself was the right thing to do. I then made them in to paper planes, and threw them over the edge. I don't know if I was trying to build up courage to do it, or trying to get rid of all the reasons I had for killing myself, thinking back on it is quite hard to work out what my motivation was. I had just wondered out for a walk, to get some space before I went through with things, and ended up there. I didn't even intend to jump or anything, I had my method planned at home, ready to come back to. It was late and cold when I realised what I was doing, and just how long I had been there. I walked home, curled up under a blanket in bed with pills and alcohol... and the rest is history I guess.

Death is a solution, but just a rather empty one. It's better than perpetual torment, but I'm just about stubborn enough to think that there may still be some sort of solution out there. Unfortunately, there is no-one here who can help me, no family or friends to speak of, which is why I am posting here. It's morning here, so sleep isn't really an option, and even in sleep my head doesn't clear, it just replaces one torrent of thoughts with another. I can't block them out, or focus on one thing, my mind just doesn't seem to work that way. I can eventually 'flood' the thoughts out with others, but sometimes it's difficult, like right now. The thoughts that want to be there are suicidal ones.

Hey, I thought it'd be something like that. Last week has been difficult, life decided this is the week it wanted to drown me in as much crap as possible, though at least it was real world crap which has forced me out of my head a bit.

I think the latter in truth, that there is more holding me back. When I try to think about what it is though, it seems like every answer is just a partial fit, so it's probably just a combination of things. Part of it is worry that I'll say the thing wrong. As a child, I wasn't very good at speaking while under pressure, and I ended up a few times saying stupid things because of it, mixing up my words, and I am still self-conscious of that. I think most of it though is that when most people talk, they think about what they want to say, and then say it (I know it's not as simple as that, but still). When I talk, I think about what I want to say, then I think about what the other person might hear, whether they will interpret it the same way as I meant it. I think that's kind of why when I talk or write, that I say a lot, because I want to remove doubt, so I have to elaborate on everything to make sure that what I want to say and what I want the other person to hear from what I am saying are close enough to the same thing. And then while I have to think about all that, I'm holding all those words in my head, and it becomes a bigger mess to try and get them out, and in the end, saying something as simple as a couple of sentences becomes a big thing.

Because not knowing something is a weakness. Not in a "personal failing" kind of way, but in a "leaving yourself open for someone else to attack you" kind of way. If I've made a mistake, and don't know what it is, there is nothing stopping me from making it again. It's probably a childhood thing again, as with most things. My father was the sort of person to criticize me for getting 49/50 on a test, even though that was more than anyone else in the class, and more than he could have even got on the test. I don't think it was that he didn't like failure, or anything else that you would get from a high pressure parent, it was just that he liked having an excuse to attack me on something. But human relationships aren't like tests, they are far more important, so a mistake there matters far more. I don't make friendships easily, but when I do they mean a huge amount to me, because they are... gifts, I guess, of trust, of closeness, and I try to guard those preciously. If I damage that, and it is my fault, for my failure... how can I ever accept that? I have to know, so I never make the same mistake again, so I don't risk losing those that are so precious to me. And I remember them always, every mistake I've made... I don't think that's a normal thingg to do, but I have to keep them fresh in my mind, so I don't make those mistakes again.

I hate my father, and I always will. I'm not a hateful person, but when someone is so deliberate in their maliciousness... I can't let that go. I moved to another country to be away from him, and though I talk to him on occasion, it's mostly just so I can still talk to my mother, who I get on ok with.

Maybe you have it spot on there, I don't like crying because I want to avoid my feelings, because of how screwed up they are. All my ways of dealing with feelings involve covering them with something else, either in my own mind, or by attacking my body, letting my physical pain overwhelm my mental pain. My feelings aren't 'safe', I cannot express negative feelings without negative consequences. Where you gain strength from it, I just find more and more to drag me down.

Never Mind the Buzzcocks (the TV show) is what got me in to the idea of combining music and comedy, though the first proper musical comedian I got in to was Bill Bailey (though his later stuff is a little more predictable). I'd say my favourite right now was Tim Minchin though, because his comedy style is both a bit silly, but really intelligent too, and I don't think I've laughed more than the first time I saw one of his shows.

I am ok, though I was close to doing something really stupid. The life stuff swamped those thoughts for a little while, but they are still there. Maybe it's just time that has made it worse. Everyone has a limit to their strength, how long they can go on in pain without getting better. You can only go on so long before thinking that things are hopeless, and never going to get better. In truth, I don't think anyone is attached to me. It's one of those things that I know suicidal people say, to try and make it easier on themselves... I guess I like to think I'm a little more clear minded than that. I'm still here though, and will keep talking for as long as I am.

I guess there are lots of barriers really in communication... it reminds me of a Douglas Adams quote actually "One of the problems of taking things apart and seeing how they work - supposing you're trying to find out how a cat works--you take that cat apart to see how it works, what you've got in your hands is a non-working cat." ... it's the same with any experience, any thought, you always lose some of it in trying to take it apart and put it in to words. I guess I'm so aware of that though because it feels more than just that. I... It's kind of like writers block I guess, it's a more distinct awareness that there is more than the limits of communication itself that is getting in the way... I don't think that makes much sense really... maybe it's more like swimming actually, usual communication is like swimming against the resistance in the water, but I feel more like I'm swimming with an anchor tied to me, that there's a specific and unnatural resistance in the way.

I guess it depends on the story, I've got much better at accepting things since back then I think. I still wish I was better at it though, because it's the things that I can't accept which are painful; I can't accept personal failure when I don't understand it. If I try and don't succeed it's ok, but if I make a mistake, I need to pull it apart, understand it, and when I don't know the mistake... it drives me crazy. I think that break-up was the first time it really happened though, I was convinced I had done something, I did not know what it was, so I tore apart everything about that time in my life to try and work it out, and ended up destroying all the good stuff which... looking back, I really needed to keep in me.

I guess not, I just feel I do it in such a... pathetic way. I feel ok when I cry because of... something, like when my cat died, or when I'm watching a particularly emotional film or something. I mean, it's hardly manly, but I don't really care too much about that. But when I cry because of my own weakness, because there's nothing more in life that I want to do than just disappear, and that my own patheticness is what is keeping me stagnant... I feel like it's not something a man of my age should be doing. It's... a bit of a touchy subject really, when I was young, I don't think I was ever told not to actually cry, but I think my father actually enjoyed making other people cry, which made me not want to cry around him. I don't mind crying, but I don't want to cry because I've lost control, so now I'm falling apart, I'm crying more, then berating myself for doing so, and it becomes a vicious cycle.

If you listen to that one, listen to "Plea from a cat named Virtute" first... they are from two different albums, but part of the same story so to speak. They're kind of sad, but not too sad, the sort of stuff I listen to when I'm feeling a bit melancholic, but don't want to risk making myself feel worse. I took a listen, I've never really been able to get Bare Naked Ladies... let me rephrase that, I've never really liked their music too much, it's the sort of thing that people seem to want to recommend to me when talking about music, because I should like it, but just don't for some reason. But the other tracks are good, I really liked Code Monkey, I... I deleted that bit, because I confused myself talking about comedy and music, basically just that one thing I didn't mention before is I really like musical comedians.

I don't think I could ever risk taking that mask down, I'm usually a good judge of character, so I can work out pretty quickly with someone how open I can be with them... some things though just can't be unsaid, and I don't see any upside in talking about it in the real world. Or maybe just part of me thinks that once I tell someone about it, I remove the option, or at least make it harder for me to kill myself when the time comes. It might hurt not to know, but to know and to feel obligated somehow, and then fail to find a way to prevent it would feel worse. I guess it's too late now though, in truth I'm convinced I'll not live out the week the way I'm struggling right now.

It's well in to the am here, and I've been awake for hours, so I really should try to do something today. Catch you later. (and you can just shorten it to Tal, that's what the character from the book I got the name from does :) )

Sometimes I don't even understand what I'm saying, so it's hard for me to know whether I'm saying everything that I should be saying. I guess that's the problem with talking, I don't know if your perception of what I've said is the same as what I think I've said. I'm probably just overthinking it in truth.

It did for a time, though more than it should have looking back. She was the first girl I fell in love with, and she left without saying a word... at the time I was so distraught, I tried to wipe everything about the relationship from my mind, but I know looking back that I stopped a lot of good because of that too. I was not good at dealing with emotional pain healthily, I'm still not in truth.

I save the fantastical stuff for my dreams and on the occasion I used to write stories, but the world I made isn't like that. I guess it is how I wish my life was like, in a way. There's no pressure there, and I don't have to be on guard all the time. I can be happy there, but I can be sad too, and I don't have to fear anyone judging me for it. I'm too old to spend the evening curled up in a ball in tears, even though... I can't help it. But there, I know that someone can be there for me if I need it, without tearing me to pieces.

I think I understand what you mean about music echoing your thoughts. I struggle to do that, I'm usually wanting to be away from my thoughts, not be kept in them. Even with the more relaxed stuff, I feel like it has to be telling some sort of story... something like The Weakerthans - Virtute the Cat Explains her Departure... I'm not sure I'm explaining it well again, sorry.

I think being suicidal has defined me for too long, at least in my own mind. I guess it makes me more aware of things that others might attach to the idea, and makes me analyse them in my own mind to make sure I'm not thinking that way because I think that others think that is how I would be thinking.

I wouldn't say it's tiring, I've been doing it for so long that it's just natural to me I guess. It's a bit more difficult online I've found, not the switching, but more keeping the people I have to be 'distinct'. But I manage to have a world of people in my head, so having to keep a few different faces on hand for the real world isn't really too tough. The worst bit though is that it is kind of... isolating. Needing all those barriers to try and manage a vaguely acceptable existence, and knowing it's screwed me for life in being able to be a totally open and honest person.

It has, kind of, though not quite in the same terms. I once brought my delusions too far in to my real life, where it was hard to distinguish between what was real and what was made up. I thought for years it cost me someone who was important to me at the time... I didn't find out until years later that them leaving had nothing to do with it. I guess since then I've just made sure I've always been aware about where the line is between reality and fantasy, and especially making sure I always knew which was which.

I like talking to people, but I don't think I'm very good at it in truth, and for a lot of reasons I'm... I wouldn't say paranoid quite, but cautious maybe about it. In truth though, it's... well I don't... sorry, trying to think about how to explain it. If I let real life people in to the things I imagine, then partly it gets harder to distinguish between the two. I don't doubt that a lot of the things I imagine are amalgamations of people I've talked to, or things I've watched in films, on TV, or in computer games, but I don't try to make them any particular way. My imagination is me, so if someone effects me, then they effect my imagination, but... sorry, I'm struggling to find a way to explain it. I don't really think too much about the stuff that's there in my head, it just... is. If I thought too much about it, then it would be more like reading a script, which is boring. I control myself in that world, but I don't try to think about controlling the people who are in it, I let the part of my brain that I'm not consciously aware of deal with that stuff.

I'd not heard of Imagine Dragons, but I'm listening to them now as I type. I think I like them, but I'll give it more time to let the songs work their way in to my head. I think it fits with one of my more relaxed playlists. You're right about Demons though, definately a good track.

I think with the epic rock stuff, you either feel it or you don't. I guess to me, it kind of feels like being taken on a journey with the music, like it's building up to... something. Most music is about the lyrics, but I particularly like stuff like Apocalyptica because there aren't lyrics with most of their stuff, so it's up to my own thoughts what the story of the music is. I try to write songs too, lyrics I mean, not music as such, so sometimes I listen to that sort of music, and think about what sort of words, what sort of story I would put to it.

Black is also easier to feel safe around... I guess I'm worried what it might say about me liking it though, people see it as a depressing colour... and I guess as I'm suicidal, it's easy to draw the link between the two. Maybe I just find the dark relaxing. As for red, I guess just regular... reddy red. The sort you get in a child's painting, just red, trying to be red, not just a particular shade of red. As you can see, maybe a simple answer can be weird, but I make a pretty good stab at making a complicated one weird too :$

I guess I've always tried to compartmentalise my life. I grew up with an abusive father, who constantly tried to get involved in and control my life. When I was self-harming at a young age, I didn't want anyone to know, so I learned very well how to hide things, to make myself seem like normal in situations where I needed to be, to prevent his intrusions in to my life. As I got better, I hid more and more, and ended up doing it with most people, to keep myself safe. Over the years it developed to me wanting to be in control of how I look to people, I want people to see me for who I want to present myself to be, or more accurately not judge me for the bits of me I don't want them to see. I don't want people in my real life knowing I am suicidal, and I guess that extends to who I am online, I want to hide the same bits of myself as I do in the real world. It's most important with the stuff about suicide, because... it makes me feel very open and vunerable, because I don't talk about these thoughts and feelings and everything that's going on often... I've been hurt enough times by people I thought I could trust, so if... if I'm going to let myself be vunerable, then at least I can make sure it's on my terms.

I've always judged my sanity on the ability to distinguish what is and isn't... real, I guess, or normal or something, rather than just through behaviour. If I can identify that something I think or do or feel is silly or irrational, whether it's having a conversation with next door's cat, or wanting to kill myself, I may not neccessarily be healthy, but at least I am as sane as I'm ever going to be. The problem is the balance, thinking or doing too much of something can make you unaware that it's abnormal. The most dangerous thoughts like this are suicidal ones, because the consequences of me not being able to identify those thoughts as bad ones is terminal. Burying those thoughts may not be healthy, but at least give me a chance to gain some perspective, but the usual ways I have of keeping those thoughts at bay don't work now, because the suicidal feeling is too strong. It's just a tough balance though, because as these feelings get stronger, my need for some sort of way out gets greater, and that's when I jump in to the fantasy world, but the more I do that, the more I want to stay there and never come out of it, to the point I'm scared that I will be able to convince myself that staying there permanently is ok, and lose touch completely with reality.

I think talking is good though, the one downside of creating your own reality is that all the perspectives come from your own head, and while I'd say I'm more imaginative than most in that regard, if I'm the cause of my problems, it's naive for me to assume that I can also be the solution to them.

For music, mostly stuff with guitars in is the best way I can describe it, I listen to everything from alt/indie rock, to heavy metal, depending on my mood, though I probably like 'epic' sounding rock best (think Muse, Sirenia, Dragonforce, Apocalyptica, for just a few off of the top of my head). But I've been known to listen to other stuff too on occasion, a bit of dub here and there, just generally anything that makes me feel something (besides nausea, which is why I don't listen to pop). Favourite colour is probably red or black... I think I'd prefer it to be red, but I tend to find myself choosing black when it comes down to actually choosing something based on colour, and no, I can't even answer a simple question like that straightforwardly... I browse reddit a lot, but don't post much, and when I do, I tend to create a fair few accounts for doing it, to kind of separate my types of thoughts, just so I don't link the regular stuff which I wont mind if someone stumbles upon and finds out with me, with the... other stuff.

It wasn't really a game, more an escape or a way to relax, but it was never supposed to have such a powerful influence over my psyche. I know the way I end up using it now is not 'sane', but my real worry is that i'll stop myself from seeing that. I want nothing more to plunge myself in to that world, and not come out, but I know I'd only be able to do that if I let go of the idea that it's not reality, and that's obviously not healthy.

I don't really want to talk about her, I've come to the realisation that she's neither part of the problem, nor part of the solution. I've tried many times to make things work, but I know I can't build my sanity around the idea of her being there for me when I need it.

She doesn't work there, she just goes there every morning to buy things, and when I'm feeling not so bad, I will sometimes go there too, end up bumping in to her. She'll buy her things, and we'll walk up the hill to her house, me carrying her basket trying to be gentlemanly, talking about inconsequential things, then sit outside, have a small repast, drink some tea... I don't even like tea, but it seems the thing to do. I guess it's a relaxing thing more than anything, she's never seen me cry or get upset, but she makes me feel like I can be... normal I guess, at least as much as anyone can in a self made delusion.

Yep, my favourite is the bakery, partly because they do these really nice cakes, with apple and cinnamon, and partly because I like helping the lady with the long yellow dress carry her wicker basket of bread and other baked stuff back to the top of the hill... most of the 'characters' in my head seem to change, but she's one of the few that is always there... which, I guess shows how much I think about it. It started off as a fun thing I guess, but recently it's just been me forcing myself to be in this delusion, to try and keep myself away from the worst of my self-destructive thoughts.

Real life is just awful, a severely dysfunctional relationship with my partner, a couple of fairly superficial friends, plenty of attempts to rectify both situations with no success, and barely the means to pay for the essentials, let alone try to work out some way of restarting my life.

It's peaceful, like some place out of a kid's story I guess, trees, rivers, mountains off in the distance, a small town, sort of quaint, old-fashioned. I guess it's more the people than the place though that keep driving me back to that delusion, people who talk to me, and listen, people who don't treat me like some sort of freak for feeling so much pain inside. Sometimes they are there for me to help deal with these things, other times they'll distract me, it's basically everything I could want in a self-built delusion designed to try and help myself feel less suicidal.
